   the `summaries` role fails peer auth (`Peer authentication failed`). `-U

---
name: feedback_kubectl_printenv_can_silently_return_empty
description: "kubectl exec -- printenv X with stderr suppressed returns EMPTY when the pod is gone, and an empty-key HMAC then fabricates a convincing 'the secret rotated' conclusion"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3c1aa6f1-c607-4eb1-9112-65ea2a8588c2
  modified: 2026-08-06T14:27:12.313Z
---

2026-08-06, debugging a prod login failure, I concluded "`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is regenerated
on every deploy" — stated confidently, with two differing signatures as evidence. **It was
false.** The sealed secret had not changed since 2026-06-22 and both replicas agreed.

**What actually happened:** prod rolled mid-session, so
`SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n ns "$OLD_POD" -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET 2>/dev/null)` hit a pod
that no longer existed. `2>/dev/null` ate the error, the assignment succeeded with an **empty
string**, and `openssl dgst -hmac ""` / `createHmac("sha256","")` happily produced a signature.
Comparing that empty-key signature against a real one looked exactly like a rotated secret.

Proof it was empty-key, and the check that should have run first:
```
HMAC("",  REDACTED) = REDACTED  # my "old" sig
HMAC(key, REDACTED) = REDACTED  # real
```

**Why:** an empty key is a *valid* input to every HMAC implementation. Nothing errors. The
failure is silent all the way to a wrong root-cause claim.

**How to apply:** never feed a shell-captured secret/token into crypto without asserting its
length first, and do not suppress stderr on the read.
```bash
SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n ns "$POD" -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET | tr -d '\r\n')
[ ${#SECRET} -eq 44 ] || { echo "BAD SECRET READ len=${#SECRET}"; exit 1; }
```
Re-resolve the pod name on every command when a rollout may be in flight — a pod name captured
minutes ago is not stable. More generally: when a measurement suddenly flips to "broken",
suspect the measurement before announcing a root cause, and prefer a `set -e` + length-assert
script over a chain of `$(...)` captures.

Related: [[feedback_verify_dont_reason_from_construction]],
[[feedback_piped_make_exit_code_is_a_false_green]],
[[reference_forged_session_cookie_shadows_real_logins]].

2026-08-06: `emrekabakci@gmail.com` could not log in to `app.lobu.ai` on **any** method
(Google, magic link, Slack). Every attempt bounced back to `/auth/login`.

**Not a server bug.** Sessions were being minted correctly — 10 rows in `session` in 24h —
and the server validated them fine. The break was entirely in the browser cookie jar.

**Root cause:** the jar held `__Secure-better-auth.session_token = 73qCtIYuVIGv…` (81 chars)
that was **readable from `document.cookie`**, i.e. NOT HttpOnly. better-auth always sets that
cookie `HttpOnly` (verified on the live `Set-Cookie`), so this one was never server-set — it
was planted by JavaScript, a leftover from a previous browser-verification session using the
`document.cookie='__Secure-better-auth.session_token=…'` recipe in `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md`.
Its token had **no row in `session`** — a dead session.

**Why re-logging-in never fixed it:** the real login sets the cookie on `Domain=.lobu.ai`,
while the planted one was host-only on `app.lobu.ai`. They coexist as two distinct cookies
with the same name, so the browser sends both. Verified with curl that **duplicates fail in
either order** — `stale; good` and `good; stale` both return `null`. So one stale planted
cookie permanently bricks logins on that machine until it is manually cleared.

**Fix:** expire the name across every scope from JS (it is not HttpOnly, so JS *can* delete
it), then log in normally:
```js
for (const d of ['','; domain=app.lobu.ai','; domain=.lobu.ai','; domain=lobu.ai'])
  document.cookie = '__Secure-better-auth.session_token=; max-age=0; path=/'+d+'; secure; samesite=lax';
```

## FIXED — PR #2558 (`fix(server): converge session-cookie scope…`)

The planted cookie was only ONE source. The production source was
`mintSessionCookieValue` (`auth/routes.ts`): it set the session cookie **host-only** while
Better Auth sets it `Domain=$AUTH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`, so `/exchange-token` and `/local-init`
(CLI / macOS menu bar deep links) manufactured the same brick for real users.

Shipped, one PR: (1) `auth/session-cookie-scope.ts` — whenever a response sets a
domain-scoped auth cookie, also emit a host-only expiry of that name, wired at the
`/api/auth/*` chokepoint so it covers every method at once **plus** `state`/`pkce_code_verifier`
(a shadowed `state` breaks the OAuth callback, not the session); (2) `mintSessionCookieValue`
now carries the zone; (3) `logger.warn` on duplicate session cookies in `multi-tenant.ts`;
(4) the doc teardown below. A bricked browser **self-heals on its next sign-in** — no
delete-on-unresolvable path was needed, and adding one was deliberately rejected as risk
without coverage.

**Trap inside the fix:** the expiry must mirror the SOURCE cookie's `Secure`, not the
request's `isHttps`. Better Auth keys `useSecureCookies` on `NODE_ENV`/configured origin,
not the forwarded proto; a `Secure`-less `Set-Cookie` for a `__Secure-` name is silently
rejected, so on divergence the whole convergence no-ops. `make review-fix` (Fable) caught
this — the first cut had the bug.

**Process fix (shipped in the same PR):** `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` now tells you to clear the planted cookie
when the verification finishes, or to drive a throwaway Chrome profile. As written, every
authenticated UI verification leaves a login-bricking landmine in the human's real browser.

Diagnosis path that worked, without the claude-in-chrome extension: drive the paired Owletto
extension (`client.operations.execute`, chrome connection **479** = MacBook / worker
`709f0d3a`; 432 = Mac mini) and `evaluate` `document.cookie` + `fetch('/api/auth/get-session')`.
Note `evaluate` returns its value at `output.value`, not `output.result.value`, and
`network_intercept_*` needs `patterns` on start and `session_id` on drain/stop — and it
returns **response bodies only**, never request headers, so it cannot show you a `Cookie` header.

Related: [[reference_scrape_pin_is_not_the_human_browser]] (479 vs 432),
[[feedback_kubectl_printenv_can_silently_return_empty]].

# Browser-driven verification (authenticated)

For any UI verification that needs a signed-in session (past the auth wall), mint a session cookie from the DB and drive the **paired Owletto extension** through the Lobu connector-operations bridge (`lobu call manage_operations`, or the SDK `operations` namespace). This runs in the user's real logged-in Chrome — no separate headless browser, no CDP, no extra browser tooling to install.

## Scope

The forged session cookie authenticates the **web admin REST mounted at `/`** (`/api/auth/*`, `/api/<orgSlug>/...`, the SPA — anything `lobu apply` and the web app talk to). It does **NOT** authenticate the **public Agent API at `/lobu`** (`/lobu/api/v1/agents/*`, `/lobu/api/v1/agents/<id>/sessions`) — that path expects a JWT bearer from the OAuth device flow (`lobu login`) or a PAT. If `/lobu/api/v1/agents` returns `401` despite a valid cookie, switch to `lobu chat` / `lobu token`.

## Pick a target

Local dev backend (with prod DB attached over Tailscale): `https://<your-tailscale-host>.ts.net:8443`. Prod: `https://app.lobu.ai`.

## Grab the secret + session token

```bash
# Local dev backend uses .env's BETTER_AUTH_SECRET
SECRET=$(grep '^BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)

# Prod uses the secret on the K8s pod
SECRET=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod \
  $(kubectl get pod -n summaries-prod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=lobu-app -o name | head -1 | sed 's|pod/||') \
  -- printenv BETTER_AUTH_SECRET)
```

Session token from the DB. With no local `DATABASE_URL` set, exec psql inside the prod DB pod (the prod DB serves both targets):

```bash
DBURL=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod <lobu-app-pod> -- printenv DATABASE_URL)
PGPASS=$(printf '%s' "$DBURL" | sed -E 's#.*://[^:]+:([^@]+)@.*#\1#')
TOKEN=$(kubectl exec -n summaries-prod lobu-ai-prod-db-1 -- \
  env PGPASSWORD="REDACTED" psql -h lobu-ai-prod-db-pooler -U summaries -d owletto -tAc \
  "SELECT token FROM session WHERE \"userId\" = '<user_id>' AND \"expiresAt\" > NOW() ORDER BY \"updatedAt\" DESC LIMIT 1")
```

## Sign the cookie

better-auth uses HMAC-SHA256, base64, then URL-encode — base64**url** does *not* validate.

```bash
SIGNED=$(SECRET="$SECRET" TOKEN="$TOKEN" node -e '
  const {createHmac}=require("node:crypto");
  const sig=createHmac("sha256",process.env.SECRET).update(process.env.TOKEN).digest("base64");
  console.log(encodeURIComponent(`${process.env.TOKEN}.${sig}`));
')
```

Cookie name is `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` whenever the baseURL is `https://` (prod and Tailscale dev qualify; only plain-http localhost uses the unprefixed `better-auth.session_token`).

## Find the Chrome connection

Browser actions dispatch to a paired Chrome extension connection (usually org `buremba`):

```bash
lobu call manage_connections --org buremba --arg action=list --raw
```

Pick the `chrome` connector with `status: active` on the machine whose browser you want to drive. `operations.listAvailable({ connection_id })` reports per-target `readiness` and `execution_targets` — use it to check the device is actually online before a long verification.

Impersonated Umit (signed his existing session token with the prod `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` per `docs/BROWSER_TESTING.md` — no DB writes, no cookie planted in any browser) and drove the exact calls the chat UI makes. I made no code changes; the modified files in `git status` are another session's.

## Yes — Umit can create a conversation, and the agent works end to end

`POST /lobu/api/v1/agents {agentId:"nasdaq-tracker", thread:…}` with his cookie → **201**, five times out of five. Then the full round trip on thread `398e05387519`:

- message accepted (`jobId 1038504`), worker `lobu-worker-api-741d0a4c4504` booted, workspace created
- `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` injected from the org-shared secret, proxy `POST /lobu/api/proxy/deepseek/...` → 200
- three tool calls ran: `query_sdk` → `operations.listAvailable`, `search_sdk`, `query_sdk` → `catalog.listInstalled` + `connections.list`
- final answer in ~46s. It correctly self-reported its own wiring: connector `market.quotes`, **connection 550 `nasdaq-market-quotes`, status active/ready, operation `quote` (1–50 symbols)**, callable via `run_sdk` → `client.operations.execute`
- transcript persisted, and the thread now shows in his `history/threads`

So the agent isn't broken. It has a working quote path it has simply never been asked to use — which matches what I said earlier: no automation bound to it, no schedule, zero `stock`/`daily-price` entities.

## The 403s in the logs are yours, not his

`POST /lobu/api/v1/agents` returned **403** five times today (18:25:13, 18:25:17, 18:51:38, 18:52:25, 18:53:04), all from `cf-connecting-ip 86.135.164.209`, `cf-ipcountry: GB` — the same machine that also talks to `buremba.lobu.ai` and holds bearer sessions against `app.lobu.ai`. Umit's client is the other one: `2a00:1d34:3403:7000:…`, `cf-ipcountry: TR`.

Reproduced deterministically: same URL, same host, same headers, **your** session cookie → `{"success":false,"error":"Forbidden"}` 403. His cookie → 201.

Root cause: chat-session creation is gated on per-user agent ownership. `agent_users` holds exactly one row for this agent — `(nasdaq-tracker, external, 4DrATUM… = Umit)` — and `agents.owner_user_id` is Umit. `requireAgentOwnership` → `verifyOwnedAgentAccess` (`packages/server/src/gateway/routes/public/agent.ts:466`) denies an org member who isn't the owner. Org membership alone doesn't grant it, so the UI happily renders the composer at `/agents/nasdaq-tracker/chat/c/<thread>` and every send 403s. Your two dead threads `b360c643695e` and `afc4818fb41a` have zero `agent_run_input` rows for exactly this reason.

Also resolves the loose end from before: Umit's client never hit `POST /lobu/api/v1/agents` in the last 90 minutes at all. He was on entity schemas, automations and operations until 18:50. The 18:42 "E2E connectivity test" runs came from an internal caller (`host: 127.0.0.1:8787`, UA `node`) stamped with his user id — not from a browser.

## Separate bug found while in there

`/watchlist` and `/$member` fire a `manage_entity` list with `parent_id: null` and get **400**: `{"error":"Invalid arguments for manage_entity: /parent_id: Expected number"}`. Hit both users' browsers (5× in 90 min). Source is `useEntitiesByType` in `packages/owletto/src/lib/api/entities.ts:630`, which passes `parent_id: options?.parentId` straight into the body — an explicit `null` survives `JSON.stringify` where `undefined` would be dropped. Same body with `parent_id` omitted → 200.

## Left behind

One visible thread in his `nasdaq-tracker` history titled *"What is your job, and which tools do you have available for pulling NASDAQ quotes?…"*, plus five empty API sessions that don't surface in the UI. I didn't delete them — that's a prod write on someone else's workspace. Say the word and I'll remove the thread and its transcript.

**Confidence: 95** on "Umit can create a conversation and the agent works" (ran the whole path as him, read the streamed tool calls and the persisted transcript). **95** on "the 403s are the non-owner member gate" (reproduced from both sides against the same endpoint, plus `agent_users`/`owner_user_id` rows). **90** on the `parent_id: null` 400 (reproduced the exact error string; the owletto call site is read from source, not stepped through). Untested: whether an actual quote fetch succeeds — I only got the agent to *describe* the `quote` operation, never to execute it.

Next actions you could pick from:
1. Have me ask the agent to pull a real quote (`AAPL, MSFT, NVDA`) as Umit — that's the last unverified link, and it would tell you whether `market.quotes` returns data or `quote_unavailable`.
2. Fix the member-can't-chat gate, or decide it's intended and make Owletto hide/disable the composer instead of 403ing on send — right now it's a dead button for every non-owner member.
3. Fix `parent_id: null` in `entities.ts:630` (drop null keys before POST) — one-line class fix, and worth grepping the other `manage_entity` bodies for the same null-vs-undefined slip.
4. Wire the actual tracker: a feed on connection 550 plus an automation with `agent_id='nasdaq-tracker'` and a schedule, since the agent already knows how to call `quote`.

Verified 2026-07-27 against `packages/server/src/mcp-handler.ts`.

**`x-lobu-agent-id` is attribution, not authorization.** `syncAgentBinding()` resolves the header (→ `clientInfo.agentId` → `clientInfo.metadata.agentId`), validates the agent exists in the org, and stores `requested_agent_id` on `mcp_sessions`. But `authCtx.agentId` is then consumed in exactly TWO places, both activity tracking: `touchAgentLastUsed()` and `touchClientActivity()`.

**Nothing reads guardrails or permissions on the MCP path.** `tools/list` is a fixed agent-facing surface (memory + SDK scripting + SQL/metrics), not derived from the bound agent. `skill://lobu` is `LOBU_SKILL_MARKDOWN`, a build-time constant identical for every session.

**Consequence:** a guardrailed agent bound over MCP has exactly the same reach as an unbound one. Whatever the token can do, the session can do. Revoke is the only real control.

**UI rule:** never label this "Act as agent" — that implies a security boundary that does not exist. Use "credit activity to". A dropdown that reads as scoping is materially deceptive UI.

**Also:** the binding is per-session — `requested_agent_id` lives on `mcp_sessions`, which has `expires_at` and is deleted. No org-level default exists for a client that sends no header. Low priority *while* it is attribution-only.

**Open decision:** either implement real scoping (which clients may bind to which agents; effective tool visibility after binding; behaviour when the agent is deleted or its permissions change; action-level audit) or keep the label honest. Do not ship the picker before this is settled.

# Who may access an agent? — problem statement + existing mechanisms

Written 2026-08-18. Evidence gathered against **prod** (`app.lobu.ai`, org `umit-unal` /
`org_GjawmpNww74`). No code was changed. This is a decision brief, not a plan.

---

## 1. The incident that exposed it

`https://umit-unal.lobu.ai/agents/nasdaq-tracker` looked broken. It is not.

- Agent `nasdaq-tracker` works end to end. Driven as its **owner** (Umit,
  `REDACTED`): session create → 201, message → worker booted,
  DeepSeek key injected from the org-shared secret, 3 tool calls (`query_sdk`,
  `search_sdk`), final answer in ~46s, transcript persisted, thread visible in history.
- The 403s in the app logs belong to a **different human**: Burak
  (`8a2D2Yb57odFHO2PldhD6n392Cf6456B`), `member` of the same org, **not** the agent's
  owner. Five 403s today (18:25:13, 18:25:17, 18:51:38, 18:52:25, 18:53:04), all from
  `cf-ipcountry: GB`. Umit's own client is `cf-ipcountry: TR` and never called that
  endpoint in the window.

Reproduced from both sides, same URL, same host, same headers, only the session cookie
differing:

| caller | `POST /lobu/api/v1/agents {agentId:"nasdaq-tracker"}` |
|---|---|
| Umit (agent owner) | **201** |
| Burak (org member, non-owner) | **403** `{"success":false,"error":"Forbidden"}` |

The UI renders the composer regardless, so a non-owner member gets a chat box whose
every send fails. Two dead threads exist in prod from this (`b360c643695e`,
`afc4818fb41a`) — URLs with zero `agent_run_input` rows.

### The asymmetry is the actual bug

Same caller (Burak, member, non-owner), same agent, same org:

| surface | result |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/umit-unal/agents` | **200** — the agent is listed |
| `GET /api/umit-unal/agents/nasdaq-tracker/config` | **200** — returns `soulMd`, `identityMd`, `guardrails`, `preApprovedTools`, `toolsConfig`, `authProfiles`, `models` |
| `GET /api/umit-unal/agents/nasdaq-tracker/guardrail-trips` | **200** |
| `POST /lobu/api/v1/agents` (create chat session) | **403** |
| `GET /lobu/api/v1/agents/nasdaq-tracker/history/threads` | **401** |

A member can read the agent's entire prompt, guardrails and tool surface, and cannot say
hello to it. Three different answers (200 / 403 / 401) for one question about one object.

---

## 2. Why: two authorization models on one object

**Surface A — org-scoped management API + `manage_agents` tool → authorizes on ORG MEMBERSHIP.**
`packages/server/src/lobu/agent-routes.ts` gates on `requireOrgId(c)` only (:559, :663, :715,
:855, :1052, …). `packages/server/src/tools/admin/manage_agents.ts` scopes list/get by org
membership (:288) and, per its own header (:1–19), lets **humans skip the write gate**
("role tier is separate"). This is what serves the 200s above.

**Surface B — agent chat / session / SSE / history → authorizes on PER-USER OWNERSHIP.**
`packages/server/src/gateway/routes/public/agent.ts:445` `authorizeAgentAccess` →
`requireAgentOwnership` → `packages/server/src/gateway/routes/shared/agent-ownership.ts:94`
`verifyOwnedAgentAccess`, which authorizes if and only if one of:
1. `session.isAdmin` (:99) — platform admin bypass, resolves no org;
2. `session.agentId === agentId` (:106) — agent-scoped session (worker/self);
3. a row in **`agent_users`** naming `(platform, userId, agentId)` resolves to exactly ONE
   org (:131, via `UserAgentsStore.findAgentOrganizations`,
   `packages/server/src/gateway/auth/user-agents-store.ts:113`);
4. legacy fallback: `agents.owner_platform/owner_user_id` matches, then back-fills
   `agent_users` (:160).

Org role is never consulted on Surface B. For `nasdaq-tracker`, `agent_users` holds exactly
one row — `(nasdaq-tracker, external, Umit)` — and `agents.owner_user_id` is Umit. Every
other human in the org therefore fails all four branches. Note also: **owning the same
agentId in two orgs denies too** (`orgs.length !== 1`), because that route carries no org
selector.

`agent_users` rows are written only by: agent create (`manage_agents.ts:379`), the
`UserAgentsStore.addAgent` reconciliation path (`user-agents-store.ts:27`), and the platform
message bridge (`gateway/connections/message-handler-bridge.ts:921`). **There is no surface
that grants another human access to an existing agent.** No `visibility`, no `shared_with`,
no invite — grep for agent share/visibility vocabulary returns nothing.

---

## 3. "Don't we already have this?" — yes, three-quarters of it

Do **not** design a new permission system. Four mechanisms already exist; the gap is
narrow and specific.

**3a. `write_approval_policies` already names agents as a resource — but only for
non-human callers.** `packages/server/src/authz/entity-policy.ts`:
- `resource_class ∈ {entity, agent_config, connector_action}` (validated in
  `packages/server/src/index.ts:1476`, :1485)
- `agent_config` rows carry **`target_agent_id`** — "read/update/delete of a specific
  agent" (:74, :846) — with a max-restrictive fold so a per-target row can only tighten
- `resolveWritePolicyDecision` (:827) → `allow | deny | require_approval`
- **the blocker:** `PolicyPrincipalKind = "agent" | "automation"` (:54, comment: *"A
  non-human principal a policy row may target"*), and `normalizePrincipalKind` (:188)
  rejects anything else. `EntityPolicyPrincipalKind` (:32) does include `"user"`, but the
  stored-row kind does not.

So the sentence *"principal P may read/update/delete agent X"* is already expressible,
storable and enforced — **as long as P is an agent or an automation.** A human is not a
principal this table can talk about. That is the hole the 403 falls through.

**3b. Role × scope access tiers exist for tools.**
`packages/server/src/auth/tool-access.ts:319` `resolveMaxAccessLevel(memberRole, scopes)` →
`read | write | admin` (owner/admin → admin, member → write, no role → read; token scopes
fold max-restrictive). Consumed by MCP (`mcp-handler.ts:472`), REST (`rest-api.ts:358`),
SDK method access (`sandbox/sdk-method-access.ts:85`), `manage_operations` list-available.
Agent chat does not consume it. Elsewhere, `memberRole !== "owner" && !== "admin"` is
checked inline (`index.ts:1287`, :2247) — a third spelling of the same idea.

**3c. Connector runs have their own resolved mode.** `connection.config.action_modes`
(`'disabled' | 'approval' | 'auto'`) via `resolveActionMode` /
`operations/action-modes.ts`, consulted before a connector's `requiresApproval` default.
Precedent for "per-object override consulted before a built-in default" — the shape an
agent-access decision should probably copy.

**3d. Entity ACL / purpose classification does NOT cover agents.** `acl_managed`,
`member_of`, `access-graph.ts`, `slack-acl-sync.ts` etc. operate on entities and edges.
There is **no `$agent` entity type** — agents are not in the entity graph, so nothing in
the ACL program answers this question today.

### Prior decisions already on record (read before re-deriving)

- `memory/authz-foundation-plan.md` — **M6 "per-AGENT dimension"**: `AccessPolicy`
  (org-chart scope, child ⊆ parent, excludes) → SDK `access` / MCP `manage_agents` / REST
  `/access` / Owletto Access UI. **Designed, not built.** ⚠️ M6 is a *different axis*:
  it bounds **what data an agent may read**, not **which humans may use the agent**. Do
  not conflate them; the naming (`AccessPolicy`) invites exactly that mistake.
- `memory/project_mcp_binding_is_attribution_not_authz.md` — `x-lobu-agent-id` is
  attribution only. Its recorded open decision is *"which clients may bind to which
  agents"* — the same family as this one, and it should be settled in the same pass.
- `memory/project_authz_foundation_program.md` — M0/M1 shipped: `AuthzScope{organizationId,
  principal, agentId?, policyVersion?}` (`authz/scope.ts`) is the existing carrier for a
  principal; `principal` is a raw user id today, verified `$member` later.

---

## 4. Decisions needed (this is what the brief is for)

1. **Is an agent an org-level object or a personal object?** Today it is stored
   org-scoped (`agents` is keyed `(organization_id, id)`), listed and read org-wide, but
   *used* personally. Pick one; the answer determines whether the default for a fellow
   member is allow-with-attribution or deny-until-granted.
2. **Which axis carries the decision?** Options, in ascending cost:
   (a) org **role tier** — reuse `resolveMaxAccessLevel`, e.g. member → may chat,
   owner/admin → may edit; (b) extend `write_approval_policies` with a **human principal
   kind** so `agent_config` + `target_agent_id` covers people too — the mechanism is
   already built and per-target exceptions already work; (c) a new per-agent grant table.
   ⚠️ (b) and (c) both change DB design and need explicit sign-off per `AGENTS.md`.
   Recommendation: **(a) as the default tier + (b) for exceptions**, because (b)'s storage,
   fold semantics, API validation and UI already exist and (a) needs no schema at all.
3. **What are the verbs?** Current de-facto set is `use/chat` (Surface B), `read config`,
   `update config`, `delete`, plus `bind over MCP` (3d) and `run as an automation`. At
   minimum `use` must become separable from `read` — the incident is precisely
   `read=allow, use=deny` inverted from what anyone expects.
4. **Should `read config` stay org-wide?** A member currently reads `soulMd`,
   `identityMd`, `guardrails`, `preApprovedTools` and `authProfiles` of an agent they may
   not use. Decide whether that is intended transparency or an over-share.
5. **Is `manage_agents` write really open to any member?** The header says humans skip the
   write gate and scoping is org membership — read as: a member may be able to `update` or
   `delete` another member's agent. **Unverified — do not test this on Umit's org.**
   Verify on a throwaway org; if true it is the more urgent half of this brief.
6. **Multi-org ownership:** `resolveAuthorizedOrgId` denies when a user owns the same
   agentId in >1 org. Decide whether the org-scoped route should pass its slug down
   (`x-lobu-org` is already resolved at `agent.ts:723`) instead of declining.
7. **UI contract:** until a grant path exists, Owletto must not render an enabled composer
   for a caller who will 403. Same rule already recorded for the MCP agent picker: never
   present a control that implies access the server won't honor.

## Do we already have this? Yes — three-quarters of it

That's the part worth saying out loud before anyone designs anything:

`write_approval_policies` already expresses *"principal P may read/update/delete agent X"*. There's a `resource_class = 'agent_config'` with a **`target_agent_id`** column for per-agent exceptions, a max-restrictive fold so a target row can only tighten, and `resolveWritePolicyDecision` returning `allow | deny | require_approval` (`packages/server/src/authz/entity-policy.ts:74`, `:827`; validated in `index.ts:1476`).

The blocker is one line: `PolicyPrincipalKind = "agent" | "automation"` (`entity-policy.ts:54`), commented *"A non-human principal a policy row may target"*. So the sentence is already storable and enforced — as long as the subject isn't a person. `EntityPolicyPrincipalKind` on line 32 does include `"user"`, but the stored-row kind doesn't. That's the exact hole the 403 fell through.

Alongside it: `resolveMaxAccessLevel(memberRole, scopes) → read|write|admin` (`auth/tool-access.ts:319`) already does role×scope tiers for MCP, REST, SDK methods and operations — agent chat just doesn't consume it. And `resolveActionMode` / `action_modes` is the existing precedent for a per-object override consulted before a built-in default.

What we don't have is any *grant path*: no `visibility`, no `shared_with`, no invite. `agent_users` rows are only written by agent-create, the store's reconciliation, and the platform message bridge. Nothing lets one human give another access to an existing agent.

Two traps the doc flags explicitly, because both invite a wrong turn:
- **M6 "per-AGENT dimension / `AccessPolicy`"** in `memory/authz-foundation-plan.md` is designed-not-built, and it's a *different axis* — it bounds what data an agent may read, not which humans may use it. The name invites the conflation.
- The **entity ACL program** (`acl_managed`, `member_of`, access-graph) doesn't reach agents at all. There's no `$agent` entity type; agents aren't in the entity graph.

The related open decision already on record — *"which clients may bind to which agents"* from `project_mcp_binding_is_attribution_not_authz.md` — is the same family and should be settled in the same pass.

## What the doc asks the next agent to decide

Seven questions, the load-bearing ones being: is an agent an org object or a personal one (it's stored and read org-wide but *used* personally); which axis carries the decision (recommendation: role tier for the default, human principal kind on `agent_config` for exceptions — because (b)'s storage, fold semantics and API validation already exist); and whether `read config` should stay org-wide, since a non-owner member currently reads `soulMd`, `identityMd`, `guardrails`, `preApprovedTools` and `authProfiles` of an agent they can't talk to.

It also carries the repro recipe (impersonation + psql), the do-nots (no new table/API without sign-off; don't rewrite `agent_users` in prod; don't plant cookies in a real browser), and appendices for the two unrelated bugs so they don't get re-discovered.

**Confidence: 92** on the mechanism inventory and the two-models diagnosis — every claim is either a reproduced HTTP status against prod or a cited `file:line` I read in this session. **Lower, ~60, on decision item 5**: the `manage_agents` header says humans skip the write gate and scoping is org membership, which reads as *any member can update or delete another member's agent* — I did **not** test it, because the only live target was Umit's real agent. The doc marks it unverified.

1. Verify item 5 on a throwaway org — if a plain member can `update`/`delete` someone else's agent, that outranks the 403 in urgency and changes the shape of the fix.
